structure: Part 2 of repos/trade-imports-ins-tests at c433e6b (main, 26 November 2026): the live-animals journey's per-page specs for transit countries, the permanent address page and the four transporter pages. Read in full: 7 specs under tests/animals/e2e/pages (transited-countries 10 tests in two describes, one without JavaScript; permanent-address 5; private-transporter 2; commercial-transporter 4; transporter 12 in two describes, one without JavaScript; transporter-add 7; transporter-add-save-cancel 2), the 9 animals page objects they drive (transited countries, permanent address, consignment addresses, party picker, party edit, transporter list, transporter type, private and commercial transporter forms), the shared page objects (party edit form, address picker results, base page, type-ahead, summary list, journey checks), the domain constants for transit countries, consignment addresses, transporters, country codes, journey party names, address types, test record names, INS transporter types, trader transporter, trader address and address details, the address book seed flow, the animals journey flow, the ui fixture and the transit countries assertion helper. The contact address page and its spec were removed from the suite (no contact-address spec or page object remains); the journey's overview task lists and Save and continue walk now end at Consignment addresses, which leads on to the review. Claims cover every test by title, every label, option, error message and control the page objects and constants name for these pages, the party pickers and party edit form as far as this part's files show them (the specs that exercise pickers and edit sit in the address-book parts), and gaps where a constant or locator is named but no test in this part asserts it.

claims.statement: Two tests in this part also run in the cross-browser runs: the transit countries page's empty-state render and the cat consignment that submits once its permanent address is answered.
claims.quote:
'renders the country search with only the intro paragraphs, the cancel link and the three buttons',
    { tag: '@cross-browser' },

claims.statement: The address book holds three types of record: an origin-or-consignor address, a destination, consignee or importer address, and a transporter.
An address book address is held against the roles it may be used for, from five: place of origin, consignor, place of destination, consignee and importer. There is no branch address role.
claims.note: The earlier extract recorded a branch address role, used by the removed contact address page; the constant no longer holds one.

claims.statement: Only the two address types ask which roles a record holds; a transporter carries no roles.
claims.quote: export const addressTypesAskingRoles = [addressTypes.originOrConsignor, addressTypes.destinationConsigneeOrImporter] as const;

claims.statement: The live-animals journey has no contact address page: both overview task lists end with Consignment addresses and hold no contact address task.
claims.note: The contact address spec and page object were removed from the suite; nothing in this part's files names a contact address.

claims.statement: Pressing Save and continue from the main import reason walks the trader through the pages in one order: import reason, commodity details, identification details, additional details, arrival details, transit countries, transporter, documents and finally consignment addresses.
claims.quote:
const stops: SaveAndContinueStop[] = [
      this.animalsPages.importReason,
      this.animalsPages.consignmentDetails,
      this.animalsPages.animalIdentification,
      this.animalsPages.additionalDetails,
      this.animalsPages.arrivalDetails,
      this.animalsPages.transitedCountries,
      this.animalsPages.transporter,
      this.animalsPages.accompanyingDocuments,
      this.animalsPages.addresses,
    ];
claims.note: The walk itself is asserted by the journey specs in another part; claimed here because it fixes where this part's pages sit in the order.

claims.statement: Continue on the consignment addresses page opens the notification's review page.
claims.quote:
await this.animalsPages.addresses.continueButton.click();
    await this.animalsPages.notificationView.heading.waitFor(pageLoadWait);

claims.statement: The consignment addresses page is headed "Consignment addresses" and introduced with "Add all the addresses that are involved in the consignment."
The consignment addresses page offers both a Continue button and Save and return to overview.
claims.quote:
await this.addCphOnAddressesHub(answers.cph);
    await this.animalsPages.addresses.saveAndReturnToOverview.click();

claims.statement: When a consignment arrives by airplane, Save and continue on arrival details goes straight to the transporter list, with no transit countries page between them.
claims.note: The walks that drive this are used by journey specs in another part.

claims.statement: When a consignment travels by railway, Save and continue on arrival details opens the transit countries page, and Save and continue there opens the transporter list.
A party picker's search is a form submit: pressing Search loads a fresh page with the results, so it needs no JavaScript.
claims.quote:
await this.searchBox.fill(term);
    await Promise.all([this.page.waitForEvent('load'), this.searchButton.click()]);
claims.note: mechanism: the picker's search helper waits for a page load after pressing Search, so the claim comes from the helper rather than an assertion in this part.

claims.statement: Searching a party picker for a country's name lists that country's addresses: every listed row reads the country, and the picker shows at most 8 with a count that matches what the address book holds.
claims.note: A shared helper read by this part; the spec that calls it (addresses-picker.spec.ts) sits in the address-book part.

claims.statement: A party picker offers the addresses held for its own role and the addresses held for no role at all.
claims.quote: (address) => address.roles.length === 0 || address.roles.includes(role),
claims.note: mechanism: the helper's own count of what the picker should offer; asserted by a spec in another part.

claims.statement: The journey's parties are seeded address book records, each held for its role: "Origin Farm" in Ennis, Ireland as place of origin; "Astra Rosales" in Bern, Switzerland as consignor; "Tech Imports Ltd" in London as place of destination; "British Livestock Ltd" in Leeds as consignee; and "Import Co UK" in London as importer.
claims.note: Seeded test data, not a specification of the data the service captures. The seed also holds seven further consignors in Austria, Ireland, Spain, Denmark (two), France and Norway.

claims.statement: Before the journeys run, the shared address book is kept to exactly one live record per seeded name, holding that record's details and roles.
claims.quote:
/**
 * Ensures one live record per journey fixture name, holding the fixture's details and roles.
 * Creates a missing record, rewrites one that differs and soft-deletes any extra with the name.
 */
claims.note: mechanism: the suite's seed upkeep for the shared organisation's address book.

claims.statement: On the consignment addresses page each party is its own section named for the role, showing the chosen address in an inset, with Change and Edit details links whose full names include the role, such as "Change consignor" and "Edit details consignor".
claims.note: Named in this part's page object; the specs that assert these links sit in the consignment-addresses part.

claims.statement: The consignment addresses page has a "County parish holding (CPH) number" section that offers an "Add a CPH number" link while no number has been given.
The permanent address's hand-entered form asks for no country, yet the saved address is shown back with "United Kingdom" as its country.
claims.quote: country: 'United Kingdom',
claims.note: Follows from the fill helper setting every field but a country, and the spec expecting United Kingdom on the consignment addresses page.

claims.statement: No test in this part proves a permanent address outside the United Kingdom, or any country list on the permanent address page.
The suite's canned commercial transporter "García Livestock Transport SL" has the approval number ES-T2-45001294, the address 43 East Hague Extension and the country Switzerland.

claims.statement: Saving a completed commercial transporter form returns the trader to the transporter list, from where Save and return to overview opens the overview.
claims.note: A journey flow step; no test in this part saves the commercial form, and the specs that do sit in other parts.
